sources.entry: vcrpy - Record and replay HTTP interactions in your tests.

summary.one_liner: VCR.py is a Python library that records HTTP interactions made during tests into cassette files and replays them on later runs.
summary.what_it_does: VCR.py wraps code in a context manager or decorator and, on the first run, records the HTTP requests and responses made through the libraries it supports. These are serialized to a cassette file, YAML by default. On later runs, matching requests are intercepted and answered from the cassette instead of hitting the network. The README says that deleting a cassette forces a fresh recording, which is how tests are updated after a server's API changes. It is a Python port of Ruby's VCR library. The README also points to the pytest-recording library for pytest fixtures.
use_cases: Speeding up test suites that call external APIs
Making tests deterministic by replaying recorded responses
Updating test fixtures after an API changes by re-recording cassettes
Mocking HTTP traffic in Python tests without hand-written stubs
notable: Records real HTTP traffic to YAML cassette files and replays it, with no hand-written mocks
Works as a context manager or decorator around test code
Deleting a cassette file triggers re-recording against the live server
Pytest integration is available through the separate pytest-recording library
caveats: The README does not list which HTTP libraries are supported; it only says 'the libraries it supports'
README is brief and gives no install or usage commands
keywords: avoid hitting real api in tests
